subject: How to introduce an exponential function in the code (formula)

messages.author: 090126e96eadd863
messages.subject: How to introduce an exponential function in the code (formula)
parts:
I am working in a spatial model in which the response data is Poisson and the mean is modelled through a sum of several components: (a) a unstructured term, (b) a spatial (Besag) component, and (c) a component specified by a particular exponential function depending on two parameters that have to be estimated. In the enclosed file you can find my model. My component in (c) is given by the function f(d_{ij}) with an exponential form (see the particular expression in the attached file).

My questions are: in which way (with which particular code) can I specify this term in (c) to be introduced together with the spatial structured bit? How can I specify that this function depends on two parameters that I need to estimate?

Thank you very much in advance for your priceless help.

Yours sincerely,

Carlos Ayyad

Hi

sorry for late reply.

The problematic part of your model is the term in (c), which for fixed
parameters in f(.) is an offset, ie can be spesified by

y ~ offset(<>) + ....


with unknown parameteres, these represents offset-'models' that can
depend on hyperparameters but do not contribute to the latent field.
this is the first time I have seen this formulation, and due to this,
INLA do not support these kind of models. I will look into some details
to see what would be required for these models to be supported, but I
guess its kind of 'lot of work'...

btw, there is a related, but not the same, concept in this report


Illian, JB , Soerbye, S & Rue, H 2012, ' A toolbox for fitting complex
spatial point process models using integrated nested Laplace
approximation (INLA) ' Annals of Applied Statistics , vol 6, no. 4, pp.
1499-1530


so if the form of the functions f(.) in your formulation is unknown and
have a simpler structure (like appearing anywhere) you can in fact
representes such models in INLA, currently not when such functional
forms are known up to some hyperparameters.
